messages:
Priya (support): Hey team — customer (Leo) hit repeated SSE disconnects during a long streaming response. They report partial chunks and then socket closed with EPIPE on our side. Posting logs and repro steps below.

Leo (customer): repro steps I used: POST /v1/responses with stream mode, then a slow consumer that reads 1kb every 10s. After ~30s the stream ends with no final chunk, client sees connection reset. Server logs show write errors.

Priya (support): Logged details from our proxy (nginx) + runtime:
```
[2026-03-14T18:12:13Z] connection=cid-12345 write_bytes=4096 err=EAGAIN attempts=3
[2026-03-14T18:12:14Z] connection=cid-12345 write_bytes=2048 err=EPIPE/ECONNRESET
[2026-03-14T18:12:14Z] runtime: aborting stream cid-12345 reason=consumer-slow buffer=1048576
```

Alex (sre): This smells like backpressure at the socket layer — kernel send buffer fills and write() returns EAGAIN, then we eventually get SIGPIPE/EPIPE when client fully closes. Do we have a threshold that aborts after X consecutive EAGAINs?

Jamie (eng-runtime): Yes, the current write path retries up to 5 times with exponential backoff, then triggers an abort if the KV cache flush / chunk delivery can't make progress. We do that to avoid holding worker threads pinned forever. The abort reason is `consumer-slow` and the code path returns 499 to upstream in some proxies.

Priya (support): Customer's machine was intentionally slow to simulate mobile poor connectivity. They need guidance and also asking if we can avoid aborting so they can reconnect and resume.

Jamie (eng-runtime): Resume-on-reconnect for SSE is tricky because we rely on ephemeral KV cache and live generation state. We can offer two mitigation paths: 1) increase socket send buffer and server-side retry window so slow clients get more time; 2) enable a short-lived persist/stream checkpoint to allow resume (engineering change).

Alex (sre): For immediate mitigation, ask customer to set TCP keepalive and increase OS-level sndbuf on their end. Also we can adjust our nginx proxy settings: `proxy_socket_keepalive on; proxy_read_timeout 300s; proxy_send_timeout 300s;` and `sendfile off` for streaming. That sometimes prevents premature close.

Priya (support): Leo, can you try running the following repro curl to see the behavior from your environment? It simulates a slow reader via pv.
```
# on linux with pv installed
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses --data-binary @prompt.json | pv -L 100 --wait | hexdump -C
```
(100 bytes/sec throttle)

Leo (customer): Ran it, got same cut after ~28s. Attached tcpdump gist: https://gist.github.com/leo/tcpdump123. Upstream proxy gave 502/499 intermittently.

Priya (support): Thanks — I'll open an internal bug. Jamie/Alex, next steps from infra/runtime: we need to log exact write syscall return codes and counters (EAGAIN count per connection) and correlate to our abort threshold. Can we make that non-breaking change?

Jamie (eng-runtime): I can add structured debug logs behind a feature flag: `runtime.sse.backpressure_diagnostics=true`. It will emit per-conn metrics: send_buf_size, pending_bytes, eagain_count. Will take ~1 day to add + roll to staging.

Alex (sre): Also recommend we expose a customer-configurable stream timeout on Dedicated/Private: allow customers to set `stream.slow_consumer_grace_period` (default 15s -> bump to 60s for this customer). For hosted tiers we can provide a safe window or request support intervention.

Priya (support): For now, workaround steps for Leo: 1) bump client read buffer and avoid tiny-read sleeps (increase from 1kb/10s to 1kb/2s); 2) set keepalive and larger sndbuf (sysctl net.core.wmem_max=2621440); 3) add retry logic on client to reconnect and fetch missing tail (idempotent requests or small resumed token window). I'll send a short KB with these steps.

Leo (customer): Ok will try the sysctl change and report. One more Q: is there a way to get partial output reliably even when we get aborted? Currently we only see last chunk dropped.

Jamie (eng-runtime): If client disconnects gracefully, we flush final chunk. But abrupt slow-consumer timeouts can cause partial truncation. Long term: we want to add on-disk spool of the last N KB per stream for resumability or a resumable streaming protocol (chunk IDs + re-requests). That's a product/engineering project.

Alex (sre): Also note we saw instances where nginx's `proxy_buffering` toggled behavior. If proxy_buffering is on for an upstream that expects streaming, the proxy may buffer and then hit memory limits — set `proxy_buffering off;` for SSE routes.

Priya (support): Action items:
- Priya: send KB + ask customer to try sysctl and curl repro (today)
- Jamie: add backpressure diagnostics behind flag and a small metric (EAGAIN spikes) (ETA 1 day to dev, 2 days to prod rollout)
- Alex: evaluate nginx config defaults for hosted SSE routes and propose safer defaults (proxy_buffering off, increased timeouts) (ETA 2 days)
- If customer needs immediate longer windows, escalate to solutioning for Dedicated config change.

InfraBot: Created ticket RW-8761 for engineering investigation (priority P2).

OpsBot: Noted: customer leo@example.com, case #CS-1127, linked to RW-8761.

Priya (support): Thanks everyone. Leo, I'll ping once we have diagnostics flag in staging and if we can offer a temporary stream window bump. Please paste the tcpdump link and exact sysctl values you tried.

Leo (customer): Uploaded tcpdump + sysctl output to the ticket. Trying the sndbuf change now.

Priya (support): Closing loop for the thread — keeping it open until we confirm customer repro fixed.

Jamie (eng-runtime): Note for followup: consider exposing an SDK helper for streaming consumers that does automatic pacing and reconnect. Could reduce these support loops.

Alex (sre): Agreed. Also log the top 10 IPs with repeated EAGAIN errors in the last 24h so we can surface hotspots.
